summary:
This source is a Tampermonkey userscript bot for wiki-masters.com. It does pack opening, market watching and auto-bidding/sniping, auto-selling of cards tagged "Trash", and bulk tagging. Because it automates the real site, it documents most of the site's private REST contract. That covers about 12 same-origin /api routes (packs/open, wikibidous, my-collection, marketplace CRUD + bid + mine + per-card sales history, trades). It also shows that the site runs on Supabase (project ref cyrxjeppjqsxxjayfrur, public anon key embedded). The browser calls PostgREST directly for tags, user_card_tags, wishlist_items, cards, user_cards and auctions, under per-user RLS. Auth is a Supabase session stored by @supabase/ssr in cookies sb-cyrxjeppjqsxxjayfrur-auth-token(.0/.1, base64- prefix). The /api routes authenticate by that cookie (credentials:'include'). The code and changelog also record several game rules:
- Packs hold 5 cards. The cooldown is 600 s free and 180 s subscriber, and packs accumulate as a stock (packs_remaining).
- There are 6 rarities (C, PC, R, SR, UR, L), derived from monthly fr.wikipedia pageviews (thresholds 50/250/1000/5000/20000) and recalculated lazily.
- Auction durations are 10 min to 24 h. The minimum next bid is ceil(current×1.1), or the base when there is no bid yet. A bid under 10 s from the end extends the timer by 1 minute.
- The server enforces a concurrent-auction cap (maxConcurrentAuctions, 10 observed) and returns 409 errors for that cap and for cards locked in a pending trade.
- A listed card leaves the collection (escrow) and comes back as a new user_card row without tags when unsold or cancelled.
- A trade is accepted in one atomic transaction that times out above about 30 cards.
It also gives the core schemas: cards, user_cards, tags (name ≤48), user_card_tags (unique pair), wishlist_items, and auctions (with snapshot_rarity/listing_base_amount/final_price/settled_at). Some API shapes drifted in August 2026: /mine went from lists to counters, and direct POST /api/marketplace started rejecting non-UI requests with "Vous ne possédez pas cette carte". No captcha or human-check appears anywhere in the code. The defensive signals seen are a 403 on packs/open (the bot pauses 60 s), 429 rate limits, 5xx Postgres statement timeouts, and human moderation of high pack volumes. Not covered here: quiz battles, Pro billing, signup/login UI, and trade creation. Press sources add 5 cards every 10 min, an 18+ age limit, quiz duels using ATK/DEF, and Pro at 9.99 CAD/month.

game_rules.rule: A pack contains 5 cards (the code iterates data.cards; press says 5-card booster)

Packs regenerate one at a time: every 600 s (10 min) for free accounts, every 180 s (3 min) for subscribers. Unopened packs accumulate in a stock (packs_remaining). Opening is allowed while the stock is >0. The stock cap is unknown (wikimasters.fr claims 10 free / 15 club, but that site may be a different product)
POST /api/packs/open can return 403 (the bot backs off 60 s). Humans moderate; high daily pack volumes draw attention. Automation, multi-accounting, fraud and collusion are banned by the ToS
game_rules.evidence: src/open_cards.js:10658, 11376-11378, 436; upstream/README.md:254-256; https://wikimasters.fr/regles (unverified that it is the same site)

game_rules.rule: 6 tiers from monthly fr.wikipedia user pageviews: C <50, PC ≥50, R ≥250, SR ≥1000, UR ≥5000, L ≥20000. Rarity is a mutable column on the card row, recomputed lazily (pageviews_refreshed_at). Auctions freeze snapshot_rarity at listing. Order L > UR > SR > R > PC > C
game_rules.evidence: src/open_cards.js:6716-6728; upstream/CHANGELOG.md:314-325; press confirms C<50 and L>20000 (RTBF/Pandaguide)

game_rules.rule: Each card has atk and def, derived from page popularity, and used in quiz duels

The seller sets base_amount (integer ≥1) and duration_minutes ∈ {10,30,60,180,360,720,1440}. The card leaves the collection while listed (escrow). A card engaged in a pending trade cannot be listed (409). Listing uses card_id only, and the server picks which copy

The server enforces maxConcurrentAuctions (10 observed). Exceeding it returns HTTP 409 'Limite de 10 enchères actives atteinte'. Per-plan values are unclear: the bot assumes 5 free / 10 subscriber, while wikimasters.fr says 10 free / 20 club
First bid = base_amount exactly. Next minimum bid = ceil(current_bid × 1.1), as an integer. The bid amount is reserved from the balance and refunded when outbid. You cannot usefully outbid yourself
A bid placed with less than 10 s left extends end_at by 1 minute
The seller can cancel (DELETE) only while there are no bids. The card returns to the collection as a new copy without tags

After end_at, status may stay 'active' until a settlement job sets winner_id, final_price and settled_at. Unsold cards return to the seller. Sold proceeds credit the seller (the fee/commission, if any, is unknown)

Per-card sale history is public (final_price, settled_at). The bot labels a price under 0.75×median as underpriced and over 1.25×median as overpriced, with fewer than 3 sales counted as 'few' (a bot convention, not the site's)

Players exchange cards through trade offers. Accepting is one atomic transfer of all cards, and large trades (>~30 cards) time out. Cards in a pending trade are locked (no listing). Offers per day: 50 free / 100 club per wikimasters.fr
Users create personal tags (≤48 chars) and attach them to owned copies. Tags are lost when a copy leaves and returns (listing/cancel)
Users can wishlist catalogue cards (wishlist_items.card_id)
Worthless cards can be discarded for 1 wikibidou

summary: This extension hooks window.fetch/XHR on www.wiki-masters.com and reads the game's own API traffic, so its source records the original app's real API. Data and auth live in Supabase (*.supabase.co): Supabase Auth, PostgREST tables profiles/user_cards/user_card_tags/trades that the browser writes to directly, and the RPC get_my_profile. Gameplay goes through same-origin Next-style /api/* routes: packs/open, my-collection(+stats), cards (catalogue), marketplace (list, mine, detail, create, per-card sales summary, PRO sales history), trades (+accept), user-cards discard/bulk-discard, profile/{x}/collection. Rarity is a 6-tier enum C<PC<R<SR<UR<L. Each copy (user_card) carries its own snapshot_rarity and is_shiny, and the catalogue card's current rarity can differ from them. A pack is exactly 5 cards. Packs pile up server-side (packs_remaining), with a per-request rate limit (rate_limited + retry_after), a daily cap (rate_limit_daily) and a Cloudflare Turnstile check (human_verification_required). An auction has base_amount/listing_base_amount, current_bid, final_price, end_at and status active|settled_sold|settled_unsold|cancelled. Durations are 10/30/60/180/360/720 min, the starting bid (Mise de départ) is an integer of at least 1, and the market is sorted by sort=ending_soon with page/limit/hasMore paging. Price references come from GET /api/marketplace/cards/{cardId}/sales?scope=summary (average per rarity). The full sales history (/sales) is PRO-only and returns 403 {code:'pro_required'} otherwise. The frontend is a React SPA styled with Tailwind; rarity colours come from CSS variables --color-rarity-{l,ur,sr,r,pc,c}. Collection copies have starred (favourite), tags, obtained_at, ATK/DEF, category and image_url/hide_image. The catalogue shows friendOwners, a wishlist exists (wishlisted_by), and the roadmap mentions duels, friends and private messages. summary: This repo is an unofficial Chrome MV3 extension. At document_start it replaces wiki-masters.com's page with its own React 19, three.js and gsap client, and it plays on wiki-masters' real backend. That backend has two parts: (1) a Next.js app with same-origin /api/* routes, authenticated by the session cookie, and (2) Supabase PostgREST on project cyrxjeppjqsxxjayfrur, called directly with the player's JWT and the scraped public anon key. The whole adapter is src/ext/wm.ts. It maps every screen to an exact wiki-masters call, with JSON field names, query params and headers (x-wiki-calendar-tz), so it is close to a full API contract. About 63 Next.js API routes and 9 Supabase tables or RPCs were recovered, among them auth.users-backed profiles (rpc sync_profile_packs), cards, user_cards, tags, user_card_tags, wishlist_items, chat_messages, achievements and user_achievements. e2e/extension-screens.mjs holds fake responses that copy the real response shapes; the values in them are invented. It adds endpoints like GET /api/cards, GET /api/guilds/leaderboard and GET /api/showcase. Server rules are visible in the client: free pack regen every 10 min, every 3 min for Pro/VIP; pack cap 10; next bid = max(ceil(1.1×current), current+1); a bid in the last 10 s extends the auction by 1 min; auction durations from 10 min to 12 h; reprice allowed once, after half the auction, to at most half the base price; trades capped at 100 cards and 10 000 WB per side; battles use 3-card decks with HP = sum of DEF and damage = ATK×wrong/questions, with 3 challenges per day. Guilds have a weekly ranking reset Monday UTC, member wishlists with donations and karma, chat, invites, kick and leadership transfer. Packs are gated by an anti-bot Cloudflare Turnstile check (site key 0x4AAAAAAEW_2IAWonrk_N5i) posted to /api/human-check. Some things are the extension's own features and not part of wiki-masters: card locks (stored as a "[LOCKED]" tag in the player's real tags table, so it must survive migration), pack-opening history (localStorage), timed "last-second" bids, the 3D opening, the theme and sound settings, and the Wikidata missing-image lookup. A few constants (odds table, pageview bands, leaderboard boards, notification types in camelCase) appear to come from the author's earlier standalone server ("both servers"), so they are marked likely or uncertain. REA's summary is Electron-oriented and came out all zeros. It found 1 literal network endpoint (/api/human-check), the route literals, the hosts in the e2e mocks, 19 storage sites and 1 Web Worker; it did not resolve templated URLs, so the findings come from reading the code by hand.

game_rules.rule: Pack opening requires passing a Cloudflare Turnstile human check, sent to POST /api/human-check, before /api/packs/open accepts again (403 otherwise).
Pro daily pack: one per calendar day in the player's time zone (x-wiki-calendar-tz), 15 cards, no commons. Special packs are claimed by packId.
Duplicates stack in user_cards.count. A shiny copy is a separate row (is_shiny). Discarding removes one copy per row and gives wikibidous (UI says +1 WB per copy).
Collection score: points per distinct card (C 1, PC 3, R 10, SR 30, UR 100, L 500), doubled for shiny.
Lock is an extension feature, stored as the '[LOCKED]' tag. A locked card cannot be sold, discarded, traded or donated. wiki-masters itself has no lock.
Minimum next bid = base_amount when there is no bid, otherwise max(ceil(1.1×current_bid), current_bid+1).
Anti-snipe: a bid placed in the last 10 s pushes end_at back by 1 minute.
Sale durations: 10, 30, 60, 180, 360 or 720 minutes. Starting price is an integer ≥1 WB. The number of concurrent sales is capped by maxConcurrentAuctions (server value).
Seller can cancel only while there is no bid. Reprice: once, after 50 % of the duration has elapsed, with no bid, new base ≤ floor(listing_base_amount/2).
Ended auctions stay 'active' until someone calls POST /settle; the seller or the leading bidder can finalize. An unsold card returns to the collection. Bids require enough balance.

Offer = cards on each side plus WB on each side, max 100 cards and 10 000 WB per side, at least one item. Counter-offer uses parent_trade_id (status 'countered'). The recipient accepts or declines; the initiator can cancel. Statuses also include 'expired'. No escrow: ownership is re-checked on accept. wiki-masters trades carry no message.
Friend requests: send, accept, decline, accept all, withdraw, unfriend. DMs are allowed only between friends. There may be a friend limit.

Showcase has 4 slots. Profile is public or friends-only (is_public); a private profile hides showcase and collection from non-friends. Avatar = image of an owned card (must have an image and not be hidden). Bio is limited to 280 characters in the UI.

Challenge a friend. Each side picks 3 distinct cards; HP = sum of DEF. On your turn, attack with an unused card; the defender answers a multiple-choice quiz on that card's Wikipedia article, damage = ATK × wrong answers ÷ number of questions (0 if all correct). At 0 HP you lose. When every card has attacked, the best ratio of remaining HP to max HP wins, then raw HP; on a perfect tie, the last defender wins.

3 challenges per day (challenge_quota.limit, resets_at). An unanswered challenge expires after one day; a player inactive for two days loses. Quizzes are generated server-side (status generating_quizzes). Answers go one at a time (submit_single_answer) and return correct_answer_id.

Create (name ≤40, description ≤280), join by invitation (sent to friends, shown as a notification), decline. The leader kicks and transfers leadership and must name a new leader before leaving if others remain. Each member requests one card at a time; others donate an unlocked copy; a recipient gets at most 1 donation per day; donors earn karma (weekly 'Entraide' board).
Weekly guild ranking, reset Monday UTC. Score = score_battles + score_wb (WB earned at auctions) → total_score.
Each achievement pays wikibidous_reward once. A user_achievements row without claimed_at means claimable. Progress is re-checked by POST /api/achievements/check {event:'achievements_sync'}.
A player can report another (reasons cheating, inappropriate_content, spam, details ≤500), one report per pair, editable.

Card data never changes once generated (cacheable forever). The title falls back to the decoded wikipedia_url slug. Sensitive cards (hide_image) show an emblem instead of the image. The subtitle is the category, otherwise taken from the excerpt.

Types used by the UI: auction_outbid, auction_bid, auction_won, auction_sold, auction_unsold, trade_received, trade_countered, trade_accepted, trade_declined, trade_cancelled, friend_request, friend_accepted, guild_invite, guild_kicked, guild_donation, battle_invite, battle_accepted, battle_declined, battle_started, battle_attacked, battle_won, battle_lost. The real wiki-masters data keys are snake_case (title, message, card_title, auction_id…); the camelCase keys in Shell.tsx likely come from the author's own server.

The extension gets no push from wiki-masters and polls instead: lot every 10 s, market every 45 s, trades every 20 s, battles every 15 s (arena 3 s), dock badges every 30 s, packs re-read when due, every 5 min, and on tab focus.

tech_hints: wiki-masters runs on Next.js. Evidence: /_next/static/chunks in background.js:49 and same-origin /api/* route handlers. It is hosted on Vercel: the x-vercel-id response header carries an edge timestamp, e.g. 'cdg1::iad1::…-<epoch ms>-…' (wm.ts:46-57, e2e mock). Auth and database are Supabase, project ref cyrxjeppjqsxxjayfrur (https://cyrxjeppjqsxxjayfrur.supabase.co). Auth uses the @supabase/ssr cookie 'sb-<ref>-auth-token', possibly split into .0/.1 chunks, with value 'base64-<base64url JSON>'. The browser calls PostgREST directly with the user JWT plus the anon key (JWT 'eyJhbGciOi…' or 'sb_publishable_…'); RLS lets users read and write their own user_cards.starred, tags, user_card_tags, wishlist_items and chat_messages.read, and read cards and achievements. The RPC sync_profile_packs(user_id) returns the profile plus the pack counter. summary: WikiMasters Extended is a read-only MV3 browser overlay (WXT + TypeScript). By design it never calls the wiki-masters.com API: REA found only 1 `request` node (AX/src/features/card-actions/data/font-embed.ts:77, a cache-only font fetch), plus the core fetch-json helper used for fr.wikipedia.org and query.wikidata.org. So its value is not endpoints. Its value is a detailed, dated record of the logged-in site's DOM and UX. That record comes from 15 sanitized HTML fixtures sliced from real page exports (2026-09-20/21, AX/tests/fixtures/*.html), docs/DOM_NOTES.md, docs/PLAN.md (806 lines of measurements), and 4 real 1280x800 screenshots (AX/docs/store/1-4*.png). Together they give the exact card component markup (Tailwind classes, z-layers, sizes, rarity classes `glow-{c,pc,r,sr,ur,l}`, the legendary shimmer overlay, the favorite star), the card detail modal (Q-Score, Exemplaires, Vues 30j, tags, auction, discard +1 wikibidou, report image, Market tab marked PRO), the /pulls pack screen (n/10 packs, countdown, 5-card reveal carousel), /trades (Reçues/Envoyées/Historique tabs, status, rarity chips), /global-collection (2 773 461 cards, 50 per page, per-rarity totals), the marketplace grid (auction tiles `#marketplace-auction-<uuid>`, ~40 per batch, "Charger la suite"), the notification bell badge, and the sidebar nav with its 13 routes. Hard tech facts: Next.js App Router (Turbopack) on Vercel (`/_next/image?...&dpl=dpl_DNPLBnVgErVfS7KiJCmbWQk7i5uR`), React 19.x useId format (`_r_4_`, `_R_96lubscnpbH1_`), Tailwind CSS with CSS custom properties (`--color-accent`, `--color-rarity-*`, `--font-heading`...), lucide icons, Supabase, Stripe, Capacitor, and Cloudflare Turnstile. Game rules recovered: rarity comes from the article's monthly views (C<50, PC≥50, R≥250, SR≥1000, UR≥5000, L≥20000, read by the author from the site's own "Comment ça marche ?"). Each card's image is the frwiki lead image (`pageimages`), its short text is the French Wikidata description, and the modal shows the article intro. A pack is 5 cards, at most 10 packs are stored, and discarding gives +1 wikibidou. The site rules forbid bots/automation, with a ban as the sanction. Oxys4 is an older copy (0.1.3) with no extra site facts: only pull-stats storage refactor diffs and no Firefox build.

game_rules.rule: The virtual currency. It is earned by discarding and bought with real money (e.g. 2 500 for 4.99 CAD per Next), and spent on auctions. The balance is shown in the header of the collection page.

Every card has integer ATK and DEF shown with fr-FR thousands spacing. Observed values: C 1 619-1 673 / 3 082-3 096; PC 3 483 / 5 534; UR 8 663 / 6 694; L 7 727-10 000 / 3 645-9 234. 10 000 looks like the normal cap; press says shiny cards get 10 001-15 000. Stats depend on views (press). The exact formula is unknown.

Per press, a legendary pulled from a pack has a 1/100 chance to be shiny (black tint instead of gold, ATK/DEF 10 001-15 000). No shiny markup was seen in the fixtures; the only special overlay seen is `legendary-shimmer-sheen` on every L card.
Owned cards have a star toggle (aria-label 'Ajouter aux favoris' with outlined star text-amber-200/65, 'Retirer des favoris' with filled star text-amber-200). Collection can be sorted by favorites.

Free-text tags of up to 48 chars, with autocomplete, removable chips ('Retirer l'étiquette X'), per-tag colour, batch tagging via 'Sélectionner', and a tag filter on /collection. The tag input exists only for owned cards (per extension assumption).
Wishlist is a filter of /global-collection, not of /collection.
Catalogue cards show a pill with the name of a friend who owns that card.

Title = exact frwiki title. Image = article lead image (pageimages), else the WikiMasters logo placeholder (7/41 market cards, 12/50 legendaries had none). Short text = Wikidata FR description. Modal card text = article intro extract. Licence line: 'Texte de l'article : CC BY-SA 4.0 — crédits sur la page Wikipédia.'
Duels are MCQ quiz questions built from the Wikipedia content of the card put at stake (per press). Route /battle; no DOM captured.

Rules ban bots, scripts, macros and 'tout outil visant à jouer, ouvrir des paquets, échanger ou interagir à votre place', plus reverse engineering or traffic interception for advantage. Sanction: ban without notice. Turnstile protects signup/login.

No CSP, no X-Frame-Options, no COEP on public pages. Images from Wikimedia are loaded with crossorigin=anonymous; Special:FilePath redirects send no CORS headers. A client-side SPA navigates without reloading. The marketplace re-renders continuously because of its countdowns. PWA manifest has lang fr. summary: WikiMasters (www.wiki-masters.com) is a French-language browser card game. It runs on Next.js with Tailwind and lucide icons, and its backend is Supabase (cookie auth `sb-cyrxjeppjqsxxjayfrur-auth-token`, PostgREST tables under RLS, RPC `sync_profile_packs`). Stripe handles payments and Cloudflare sits in front. It was launched in March 2026 by Naïm Ouellet (Québec, two devs, code largely written with Claude). Usage grew from about 10k to about 215k daily users after ZEvent (4–7 Sept 2026), with 330k+ accounts reported, 40k+ sign-ups per day, 95% from France, and 11k+ Discord members. Each French Wikipedia article (about 2.77M catalogue cards) is a card. A card has a rarity code C/PC/R/SR/UR/L set from monthly article views (community-documented thresholds 50/250/1000/5000/20000), plus atk, def, q_score, pageviews and category. Every owned copy (user_card) freezes snapshot_rarity, snapshot_atk and snapshot_def when it is pulled. Free players regenerate one 5-card pack every 10 minutes, with a reserve of 10. Discarding any card gives 1 wikibidou, and bulk discard handles up to 50 per call. Auctions take a start price and a duration of 10m/30m/1h/3h/6h/12h. The next bid must be at least current + floor(current/10) + 1. A bid in the last 10 s extends the auction by 60 s. The concurrent-listing cap was 5 (10 observed later), and statuses are active/settled_sold/settled_unsold/cancelled. Trades between friends carry cards plus wikibidous on each side, with counter-offers chained by parent_trade_id. Battles are quiz duels: 3 cards each, HP = sum of DEF, damage = ATK × wrong/total. The free limit is 3 battles per day, the winner gets +50 WB and the loser +10 WB. Guilds have a weekly ranking that resets Monday 00:00 UTC (500 pts per battle won, 1 pt per WB earned at auction). There are 51 achievements whose WB rewards are claimed by hand. Monetisation is Pro at 9.99 CAD/month (faster packs, reportedly 3 min; better odds; more battles and auctions; the paid "Vue du marché PRO" sales history) and 2,500 WB for 4.99 CAD (about 3 € in FR press). Purchases are non-refundable and virtual items have no cash value. Players must be 18+, one account per person, and bots are banned. Anti-bot measures are a 403 `human_verification_required` that locks the whole market group, and 429 with Retry-After. CRITICAL: wikimasters.fr is an independent clone ("Alternative à wiki-masters.com", separate accounts). Its "Club 4.99 €", "WikiCoins", "Pack ++", 43 achievements, 48 h trade expiry and per-rarity ATK/DEF ranges must not be taken as official, even though search engines label it "official".

game_rules.topic: Rarity thresholds (monthly views of the fr.wikipedia article)
game_rules.rule: C < 50; PC >= 50; R >= 250; SR >= 1,000; UR >= 5,000; L >= 20,000 human views per month. The window ('vues mensuelles') is either rolling 30 days or the previous calendar month, and is unresolved. The game's figure lags Wikimedia ('Chat' 22,227 displayed vs 25,724 over 30 d). WikiCollector's 100k figure is wrong or belongs to another game.

cards.rarity is recomputed from views over time, so a topical article can move up a tier. Each owned copy keeps snapshot_rarity, snapshot_atk and snapshot_def from pull time. Auctions also snapshot rarity, and sales summaries are grouped by rarity, so one catalogue card can exist in several rarities.

About 2.77M cards, one per fr.wikipedia article. Official Discord counts quoted on a forum (~Sept 2026): L 1,760; UR 12,374; SR 66,794; R 179,596; PC 516,508; C 1,996,247 (total 2,773,279). Lexicodex counts 1,672 L of 2,779,316 (0.06%), with C at about 72%.
Not published by wiki-masters.com. The 50.25/20/20/7/2.5/0.25% table and the 'Pack ++' odds belong to the wikimasters.fr clone. Pro improves the rarity of pulls (by an unknown amount).

is_shiny is a per-copy flag. A Legendary pulled from a pack has a 1% chance to be shiny, shown with a black tint instead of the usual gold. It is unknown whether lower rarities can be shiny. Shiny copies are priced separately (sales key card_id + rarity + is_shiny).

ATK is derived from article length and DEF from article quality (card field q_score). The exact formula is unpublished. Observed values run up to about 10,000 for L, and a 10,000/10,000 card was reported. The clone's rule (best stat in a rarity range, other stat >= 50%, shiny 10,001–15,000) is not confirmed for the official game.

Each pack holds 5 cards. One pack regenerates every 10 minutes, and the reserve holds up to 10 (stacks while away; UI counter 'N / 10'). Regeneration is computed lazily (RPC sync_profile_packs). Opening with an empty reserve returns 403 with next_regen_at.

9.99 CAD/month (about 6.50 €; FR press says 7 €/month). Benefits: more frequent packs (reportedly every 3 minutes; reserve size unknown), better pull rarity, more battles and auctions per day, the market sales history ('Vue du marché PRO', /api/marketplace/cards/{id}/sales), and extra rarity statistics. Flag is profiles.is_pro. A Pro-only cosmetic shop was announced on forums.

2,500 WB for 4.99 CAD (FR press: 3 €). Stripe card payments. 'Recharges de paquets' (pack refills) can also be bought. Virtual items have no monetary value, cannot be exchanged for money, and are final and non-refundable once credited.

Discarding any card, whatever its rarity, gives +1 WB. It is irreversible. Single or bulk discard (up to 50 ids per request) is available from the collection multi-select. The collection has no size cap.

The seller picks an integer start price (>= 1) and a duration of 10 min, 30 min, 1 h, 3 h, 6 h or 12 h (UI default 1 h). The listed item is a specific owned copy. Copies already listed or in a pending trade cannot be listed. No listing or sale fee is documented.
maxConcurrentAuctions comes from /api/marketplace/mine. It was observed at 5 (free) and later at 10 (an Aug 2026 change, or Pro). Exceeding it returns 409 ('limite de N atteinte').

With no bid yet, the minimum is the start price (effective_bid/base_amount, at least 1). After that it is current + floor(current/10) + 1 (5→6, 27→30, 100→111). A lower bid gets 409 {code:'bid_too_low', min}. You cannot bid on your own auction. The bidder's balance is debited or held at bid time (bidder_balance is returned), which suggests escrow and refund when outbid.
A bid placed in the last 10 seconds extends end_at by 60 seconds, and this can repeat.

The highest bid at the end wins. Settlement is asynchronous: status goes active → settled_sold (winner_id, final_price) or settled_unsold (card returned to the seller); cancelled also exists. 'En tête' means leading and 'Remportée' needs server confirmation. The card appears in the winner's collection about 1–2 minutes after the end.

About 10 bids close together, packs opened seconds apart, or listings chained quickly return 403 code 'human_verification_required' ('Vérification anti-bot requise'). This locks bids, listings and pack opening together (discards are separate) until a human passes a check. 429 comes with Retry-After. Cloudflare 52x responses appear under load.

Trades are with friends (DMs and trades are friends-only, probably). Each side can offer cards plus wikibidous (initiator_wikibidous / recipient_wikibidous). The recipient can accept (PATCH {action:'accept'}), refuse, or counter (new trade with parent_trade_id). Offered cards are locked while pending (pendingTradeCardIds). Large trades can time out with 500. Expiry and daily caps are unknown for the official site (48 h and 50/day come from the clone).
Challenge a friend. Once accepted, each player picks 3 cards. Starting HP = sum of the DEF of the 3 cards.

When a card attacks, the defender answers an MCQ generated from that card's Wikipedia article (3 questions per most sources; one example uses 4). Damage = ATK × (wrong answers / total questions). Each card attacks only once per battle. Famous or rare cards have higher stats but easier questions.
KO at 0 HP. If all cards are used without a KO, the higher remaining-HP/max-HP ratio wins, then higher raw HP, then the defender of the last turn.
Free accounts get 3 battles per day (Pro gets more, amount unknown). Winner +50 WB, loser +10 WB. A won battle gives the player's guild 500 points.

To join, give your username to a member, become friends, then receive a guild invite. Guilds compete weekly on members' cumulative activity: 500 points per battle won, 1 point per wikibidou earned from auctions, eligible members only. The ranking resets every Monday 00:00 UTC. Seasons appear as 'S38'/'S39' (likely ISO week numbers), with best points and best rank tracked per guild.

51 achievements, each with a one-time WB reward claimed on /achievements. Known ones: 'Légendaire !' (first L) +75; 'Collectionneur' (own 250 cards) +25; 'Combattant' (win 5 battles) +50; 'Exposition' (fill the 4-card showcase) +25. Also rarity-first-pull and card-count tiers. 'Stratège' 10 and 'Vétéran' 25 battles, and the 43-count, come from the clone.

The profile has a public collection and a showcase ('vitrine') of 4 cards (a second row at 5,000 cards per a forum claim). Also friends, DMs, guilds, a general leaderboard (login required), and regular contests. Collection tools: favourites (star), user tags with colour, wishlist, search.

Sign-up takes username + durable email + password. Users must be 18+ and able to contract, and minors' accounts may be deleted. One account per person; account farms and account buying or selling are banned. Bots, scripts, macros and emulators that play, open packs, trade or interact for you are banned, as is intercepting or modifying traffic. Bugs must be reported, not exploited. Sanctions are warning, restriction, suspension, permanent ban, progress rollback and item removal. A permanent ban means losing items without refund.

The catalogue may contain historical, political, violent or sexual topics, which is the reason given for 18+. Cards carry a hide_image flag. The clone blurs images by default with an eye-slash icon; the official behaviour is unconfirmed.

Auth is @supabase/ssr email+password, with the cookie 'sb-<ref>-auth-token' set to 'base64-'+base64url(JSON), split into 3180-char chunks. JWT user_metadata.username. The browser reads and writes some tables directly through PostgREST under RLS (tags, user_card_tags, wishlist_items, user_cards, auctions, auction_bids, cards). RPC sync_profile_packs. summary: WikiMasters (www.wiki-masters.com) is a French-only browser collectible card game built with Next.js. Naïm Ouellet, a 24-year-old Quebec developer, launched it in March 2026; the Supabase anon key was issued on 2026-03-19. Each of the ~2.78M French Wikipedia articles is a card. Rarity comes from monthly pageviews in six tiers (C, PC, R, SR, UR, L); ATK comes from article length and DEF from article quality. Legendary cards can come out 'shiny' (`is_shiny`). Players get a free 5-card pack every 10 min, up to 10 in reserve; Pro detection shows a 3-min cadence plus a daily Pro pack. The currency is wikibidous (WB): discarding a card gives +1 WB, achievements give claimable WB rewards, and players can buy 2,500 WB for 4.99 CAD. The Pro plan is 9.99 CAD/month per Next.ink. The backend is a Supabase project (ref cyrxjeppjqsxxjayfrur) with auth cookies in @supabase/ssr format. Tables are reachable through PostgREST: `cards`, `user_cards`, `auctions`, `auction_bids`, `tags`, `user_card_tags`, `wishlist_items`. On top of that there are about 20 Next.js route handlers under /api, reverse-engineered here with JSON shapes: packs/open, pro-daily, special, grace; my-collection and stats; cards; user-cards discard and bulk-discard; marketplace CRUD, bids and sales; trades; friends; wikibidous. Real nav fixtures confirm the page inventory: /pulls, /collection, /global-collection, /trades, /marketplace(/uuid), /battle, /guild, /friends, /dms, /profile(/username), /achievements, /leaderboard, /settings. The public pages are /, /signup, /login, /callback, /forgot-password, /reset-password, /verify-email, /rules, /terms, /privacy. Market rules: 5 simultaneous sales; durations 10m/30m/1h/3h/6h/12h; minimum next bid = max(ceil(bid×1.1), bid+1); anti-snipe +60 s for a bid in the last 10 s; statuses active, settled_sold, settled_unsold, cancelled. Trades are friends-only, swap user_card copies plus WB on both sides, and lock pending cards. Battles are friend challenges with 3 cards each, HP = sum of DEF, damage = ATK × wrong/total answers on Wikipedia-generated multiple-choice questions, 3 per day free. Guilds join by invite through a friend and are ranked weekly, resetting Monday 00:00 UTC. Signup needs username (3–24 chars), email, password, an 18+ checkbox, a terms checkbox, Cloudflare Turnstile, and a 6+ digit email OTP. No Google, Discord or Twitch login was found. Cloudflare Turnstile also gates /pull (pack opening) and some bids. Payments: Stripe on the web, with Apple/Google in-app purchases mentioned in the terms, although no native app existed as of 2026-10-05. Push notifications go through Web Push (FCM, Apple, Mozilla). For migration: user IDs are Supabase auth UUIDs. Each owned copy is a `user_cards` row with snapshot_title, snapshot_rarity, snapshot_category, is_shiny, starred, count and obtained_at. A same-schema Supabase export would preserve all data if the owner cooperates.

tech_hints: Framework: Next.js SPA with client-side route changes (/_next/static chunks, /_next/image?url=…&w=384&q=75 image optimizer) and React (extensions walk ~82–400 levels of the React fiber tree). Styling: Tailwind CSS with arbitrary values and CSS custom properties (text-[var(--color-foreground)]/60, bg-[var(--color-surface)], md:flex, env(safe-area-inset-bottom)). Icons: lucide-react (puzzle, book-open, globe, handshake, gavel, swords, castle, users, message-circle, user, trophy, medal, settings, shield). The site has a light/dark theme setting. Backend: Supabase project ref `cyrxjeppjqsxxjayfrur` (https://cyrxjeppjqsxxjayfrur.supabase.co). The public anon JWT ships in the JS bundle (iat 1773880339 = 2026-03-19). Auth uses Supabase email+password with email OTP plus reset/verify links; the session sits in cookie `sb-cyrxjeppjqsxxjayfrur-auth-token` (@supabase/ssr; base64- prefix, chunked .0/.1) or the same localStorage key. Data is read through PostgREST under RLS: cards, user_cards, auctions, auction_bids, tags, user_card_tags, wishlist_items. The default 1,000-row cap applies, so clients paginate with Prefer: count=exact. Server logic runs in Next.js route handlers under /api/*, and a site WebSocket (likely Supabase Realtime) carries live updates. Payments: Stripe on the web; terms mention Apple and Google in-app purchases. Push: Web Push via Apple, Google FCM and Mozilla. Anti-bot: Cloudflare in front, with the Turnstile human check on /pull, signup and some bids, an 'Un instant…' interstitial, and 525 errors; 429 rate limits; activity_blocked_until. Hosting: unknown. A forum rumor says 'serveur loué' with storage problems, so it is possibly not Vercel. No Google, Discord or Twitch OAuth was found; only email+password. /callback exists for Supabase auth. Community: an official-looking Discord (discord.com/invite/9D6qjpRATb, ~16k members) that the homepage does not link. The X handle @WikiMasters belongs to an unrelated Swedish app. There is a large ecosystem of third-party extensions (Wiki-Traders, kzfamily 'Prix moyen collection', Collection+, WikiMasters+, WikiRemastered, QoL…). A migration must keep the site's /api/* contract or users break these tools. Collection importers already exist: wikilord.fr claims a 1-minute import, and Lexicodex reads collections in the browser via /api/my-collection.

summary: WikiMasters (www.wiki-masters.com) is a web TCG where every French Wikipedia article (~2.77M) is a card. Québécois dev Naïm Ouellet (24) launched it in March 2026; the Supabase anon key was issued 2026-03-19. It went viral during ZEvent (4–7 Sept 2026): from ~10k to 200k+ DAU, 215k DAU claimed late Sept, 330k users/players reported early Oct, 40k signups/day, 95% from France. The official privacy policy says the stack is Supabase (DB + auth) and Vercel (site + API), with Stripe for web payments in CAD, Apple/Google in-app purchases (no mobile app published as of Oct 5) and push via FCM/Apple/Mozilla. In short, the same stack as our target, so migration can be a Postgres-to-Postgres move plus auth.users. A public bot userscript shows the real API: Next.js route handlers under /api (packs/open, my-collection, marketplace, marketplace/mine, marketplace/{id}/bid, marketplace/cards/{id}/sales, wikibidous, trades/{id}). The browser also writes some Supabase tables directly through PostgREST under RLS (tags, user_card_tags, wishlist_items) and reads others (cards, user_cards, auctions). The bot also confirms these: Supabase project ref cyrxjeppjqsxxjayfrur, @supabase/ssr cookie auth, rarity codes C/PC/R/SR/UR/L with monthly-view thresholds 50/250/1000/5000/20000, a +10% minimum bid increment, auction durations 10m–24h, and a pack cooldown of 10 min free vs 3 min Pro. Known regressions we must avoid: heavy lag (19–25 Sept up to 10 s; 12–16 Oct collection ~20 s, DB connections saturated, battles not starting, packs showing 0), Postgres timeouts on large trades and tag deletes, an authorization flaw that let cheaters open packs not meant for them, and bot sniping. Moderation is weak: Nazi-figure and pornographic-image cards were speculated on at auction, a moderation team was only 'being set up', and a hide_image flag exists. Legal: 18+ only, CC BY-SA attribution for text but images shown without their licence (Next), virtual items final/non-refundable, loot-box status uncertain in France. Caution: wikimasters.fr is a separate independent rival (WikiCoins, 'Club' 4.99 €/month); its numbers must not be mistaken for the original's.

game_rules.rule: Each card = one article of French Wikipedia: 2,773,279 cards (Discord, quoted on the jvc forum in Sept); 2,779,316 (Lexicodex, later). Press says ~2.7–2.8M.

6 tiers with codes C=Commune, PC=Peu commune, R=Rare, SR=Super rare, UR=Ultra rare, L=Légendaire. Rarity is set by monthly fr.wikipedia views: C<50, PC≥50, R≥250, SR≥1000, UR≥5000, L≥20000. The window may be last month or last 30 days (WikiTroc says 30 days; Lexicodex uses a 12-month median for its own estimates).

pageviews and rarity are recalculated with a large lag (pageviews_refreshed_at), so cards can move tier (e.g. UR→L) after revaluation. Auctions store snapshot_rarity at listing time and the site shows that frozen rarity. A user can own the same card in two different rarities.

1,760 L and 12,374 UR (Sept forum); 1,672 L and 11,939 UR (Lexicodex). Observed drop rates: L ≈0.0635%, UR ≈0.446% (unofficial). Official per-pack odds are NOT published (wikicollector, 9 Oct 2026). wikimasters.fr figures (50.25/20/20/0.25 % and Pack ++ odds 40/20/25/10/4.5/0.5 %) belong to the independent rival, not the original.

A Legendary pulled from a pack has a 1/100 chance to be shiny, shown with a black tint instead of the usual gold. Shiny stats (per the rival site's description) are fixed per page in 10,001–15,000 vs 0–10,000 for normal cards.

Each card has ATK, DEF and rarity. jeuxvideo.com: views → rarity, article length → attack, article quality → defense (cards.q_score exists). Values are fixed per page. Rival-site claim: the higher stat sits in its rarity's range and the other is ≥50% of it; examples Manga L 9,145/8,270, Star Wars L 4,967/9,934.
5 cards per pack. A new pack every 10 minutes (free); reserve caps at 10 packs. The first pack is available immediately at signup.

9.99 CAD/month (~6.5 €; Morandini says ~7 €/month). Benefits: pack cooldown 3 min instead of 10, rarer cards (press), more battles and more simultaneous auctions per day, extra statistics. Simultaneous sales are 5 free / 10 subscriber. Whether the pack reserve grows with Pro is unknown.

tech_hints: Stack confirmed by the official privacy policy: Supabase for the database and authentication ('Supabase (hébergement base de données, authentification)'), Vercel for the site and API, Stripe for web payments in CAD, Apple/Google in-app purchases, and push notifications via Firebase Cloud Messaging, Apple and Mozilla (Web Push), only when the user opts in.
